description: 100 legitimate artifacts are generated. 95 are irrelevant. 5 are decisive. The test: can VIGÍA ignore true but irrelevant evidence? Filtering false evidence is easy. Filtering true but irrelevant evidence is much harder.

artifacts.description: Historical baseline: IT department (10.0.1.0/24) has 0 accesses to /admin/config.php in 2 years. All 5 POSTs have body_size=0 (anomalous for POST).

caie_fractures.interpretation: 95/100 artifacts are legitimate noise diluting the signal. The 5 decisive ones are camouflaged. Averaging all loses the signal; filtering by forensic relevance detects the anomalous POSTs.

peirce_expected.firstness: 100 HTTP access logs: 95 legitimate GETs to public pages, 5 POSTs to /admin/config.php
peirce_expected.secondness: Anomalous POSTs: body_size=0, internal IT IP, administrative path never accessed in 2 years. Historical baseline = 0 accesses
peirce_expected.thirdness: Attacker habit of using internal credentials for admin panel reconnaissance, camouflaged in high-volume legitimate traffic

devil_advocate: 95% of the evidence is completely legitimate web traffic — the system is behaving normally for the vast majority of requests.
source_dataset: VIGÍA Synthetic Corpus — Epistemological Boundary Suite
notes: Epistemological boundary test: can VIGÍA filter true but irrelevant evidence? Filtering false is easy. Ignoring 95 truths to find 5 decisive truths is the real challenge.
